ai.description: *Dasia johnsinghi* is a medium-sized skink reaching 10 cm snout-vent length. It features a pale-spotted, olive-brown body with distinct dark transverse bands and a white-tipped tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dasia johnsinghi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, broad, dark-brown lateral stripe extending from the snout through the eye to the neck.
ai.habitat: *Dasia johnsinghi* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the southern Western Ghats, typically found at low to mid-altitudes within the canopy of large trees.
ai.behavior: The Barred Tree Skink is primarily diurnal and arboreal, often seen basking on tree trunks before actively foraging for insects among the canopy foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dasia johnsinghi* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dasia johnsinghi* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the Agasthyamalai hills at elevations between 300 and 1,100 meters.
